chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who informed him, from Abū Baṣīr who said:

I heard Abā Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, divine revelation was withheld from Mūsā ibn ʿImrān (peace be upon him) for thirty mornings, so he ascended a mountain in al-Shām which was called Arīḥā, and said: "O Lord, why have You withheld Your revelation and Your communication from me? Is it because of the sin I committed? Then here I am before You, so do with me as You please! And if You have withheld Your revelation and communication from me due to the sins of the Banī Isrāʾīl, then Your pre-eternal forgiveness [is sufficient]." So Allah revealed to him saying: "O Mūsā, do you know why I chose you for My revelation and communication among My creation?" He said: "I do not know that, O Lord." He said: "O Mūsā, I examined My creation, inspecting them, but did not see anyone among them as intensely humble as you. That is why I chose you for My revelation and communication among My creation." He (the Imam) said: "When Mūsā (peace be upon him) used to pray, he did not turn aside [from his prayers] until he placed his right cheek on the earth and his left cheek upon the earth."'
ai.seo_question: Why was divine revelation withheld from Prophet Moses for thirty days according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the divine attribute of *Tawadu* (humility) as the primary criterion for prophetic selection, distinguishing Moses (AS) not by his merits but by his profound self-abasement. The text highlights a unique physical manifestation of this spiritual state, where Moses would press his right cheek to the ground during prayer, a practice reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Khushu* (devotion) and the rejection of pride even in the presence of direct divine speech. This account serves as a theological counterpoint to the Israelites' arrogance, reinforcing the Shia scholarly view that true closeness to God is achieved through humility rather than status.
